sections.heading: A more flexible way to get senior marketing leadership.

items.a: A fractional CMO gives a business access to senior marketing leadership for part of the time and for as long as the role is useful. The work can include positioning, ICP, go-to-market strategy, demand generation, pipeline, measurement and sales alignment. Sometimes the problem sits inside marketing; sometimes marketing is where a product, proposition or operating problem becomes visible.

items.q: How is a fractional CMO different from an agency?
items.a: An agency usually delivers a defined scope of work. A fractional CMO takes senior responsibility for the commercial marketing decisions and stays accountable for joining the work together, bringing the right specialist operators around the problem where they are needed rather than delivering a single service.

items.q: When does a fractional CMO make sense?
items.a: When the business needs CMO-level decisions now but does not yet need, or is not yet ready for, a permanent executive. That often applies when founders are still carrying senior marketing decisions, when growth has slowed and more activity is not fixing it, or when GTM investment is increasing without enough confidence in where it should go.

items.q: What does CommView typically work on?
items.a: Engagements are shaped around the business problem rather than a generic list. Depending on the situation we can own positioning and ICP, go-to-market, growth and demand, pipeline and sales alignment, measurement and investment, and the team and operating rhythm.

items.q: Can you work with our existing team?
items.a: Yes. We give internal teams and specialist partners clearer priorities, decisions and accountability, and bring in specialist operators across GTM, Growth, Product and Operational AI where the problem requires them, rather than replacing good people.

items.q: How long do engagements usually last?
items.a: It depends on the problem and the stage. The objective is not to keep a fractional role forever. It is to give the business the leadership it needs for the stage it is in, and to agree the scope and expected outcomes before the work starts.
